newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures up, led by palladium.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures up, led by palladium.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended higher on Tuesday, led by palladium, as lingering uncertainty over Russian exports of white metals and a weak yen supported the market, traders said.

The benchmark December palladium futures contract ended up 18 yen at 543 yen, after hitting its daily 22 yen per gram limit just ahead of the close. Only February was lower, while other prices were four to 16 yen higher by the close.
Gold futures ranged from one to seven yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark December settling up four yen at 1,371 yen.
Traders said worries about the health of China"s paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had had little impact on the precious metal futures market.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $345.90/346.50 per ounce at 0805 GMT, against Monday"s London fix of $344.10 and Tokyo"s Monday close of $343.90/344.20.
"In palladium futures, private investors, who took profits earlier in the day, bought again later," one trader said.
Traders said that until a time schedule for talks between Japan-Russia on export contracts for platinum group metals became clear, bullish sentiment in palladium would continue.
Traders said gains in palladium futures spilled over into platinum, silver and finally gold on Tuesday.

A widespread perception that the dollar will stay strong against the yen, was also considered bullish for the market. Platinum futures ranged from five yen to 22 yen per gram firmer, with most-active benchmark December ending up 22 yen at 1,452 yen.
Silver futures ranged from 0.2 yen per 10 grams weaker to 3.4 yen higher. Benchmark December silver was up 3.4 yen at 211.0 yen.
